proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  By Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}attainable\text{-}law\text{-}class}\), \(Q\) satisfies
consistency, ignorability, bounded outcomes, overlap, propensity H\"older
smoothness, control-regression H\"older smoothness, and CATE H\"older
smoothness, which are all the nondensity member conditions in Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}law\text{-}class}\).  It remains only to verify
the two density conditions in the latter definition.  Assumption
\(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}design}\) gives
\[
 f_Q(x)=1
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in\mathcal X.
\tag{1}
\]
The declared ranges \(0<\underline f\le1\) and
\(1\le\overline f<\infty\), together with (1), imply
\[
 f_Q(x)\le\overline f
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in\mathcal X
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 f_Q(x)\ge\underline f
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }
 x\in x_0+[-r_0,r_0]^d.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus \(Q\) also satisfies the global density upper bound and the anchor
local density lower bound.  Every member condition in Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}law\text{-}class}\) now holds, so
\(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Since \(Q\) was arbitrary,
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\subset\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\) be the collection of all replacement
\((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private random intervals \(C\)
satisfying
\[
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C\}\ge1-\eta,
\]
and define
\[
 \mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}})
 =\inf_{C\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}}
   \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
   \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}(C)].
\]
If \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\) and \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), then there are
constants \(c,C>0\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), depending only on the fixed
class constants and \(\eta\), such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 c\left[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \vee\left\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\right\}\right]
 &\le \mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}})\\
 &\le C\min\left\{
 1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},
 1\wedge\left[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}
       \vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\right]
 \right\}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
The minimum in (1) can be a strict polynomial improvement over the
higher-order interval alone.  In particular, if \(q\ge\gamma\),
\(\beta<\gamma<2\beta\), and
\(N_{\mathrm{priv}}=n^{c_{\mathrm p}}\), where
\[
 0<c_{\mathrm p}<
 \min\left\{\frac{\gamma+2d}{2\gamma+d},
             \frac{\beta+d}{2\beta+d}\right\},
\tag{2}
\]
then, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the two entries of the upper
minimum are respectively
\[
 n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\beta/(\beta+d)},
\]
and their ratio, second over first, converges polynomially to zero.  This
is the best certified bracket here for the attainable class; it makes no
claim that the full-class open frontier is sharp.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We first adapt the two-law argument in Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}class\text{-}ordinary\text{-}lower}\) to
intervals honest only on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  Use exactly the
bump \(\varphi\), constants \(p_*=\min\{1/4,L_\mu/2\}\) and \(a_*>0\),
and functions
\[
 g_h(x)=a_*h^\gamma\varphi((x-x_0)/h)
\tag{3}
\]
constructed in that theorem.  Its H\"older calculation gives
\[
 g_h\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L_\tau;\mathcal X),
 \qquad 0\le g_h\le p_*/2,
 \qquad g_h(x_0)=a_*h^\gamma,
\tag{4}
\]
for \(0<h\le r_0\).  Let \(Q_0,Q_h\) be the same full-data laws: under
both, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal X\),
\(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\kappa)\), and \(A\) is
conditionally independent of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \(X\); under \(Q_0\)
the two conditionally independent potential outcomes are Bernoulli with
mean \(p_*\), whereas under \(Q_h\) their respective conditional means are
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_h}[Y(0)\mid X=x]=p_*,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{Q_h}[Y(1)\mid X=x]=p_*+g_h(x).
\tag{5}
\]
In both laws set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).

We verify the stronger membership needed here.  The last construction
gives consistency.  The specified conditional independence gives
ignorability.  The potential outcomes have the common support
\(\{0,1\}\), and (4) gives
\[
 0<p_*\le p_*+g_h(x)\le3p_*/2\le3/8<1,
\tag{6}
\]
so the Bernoulli laws are well defined and bounded outcomes holds.  Since
\(0<\kappa<1/2\), the constant propensity satisfies
\[
 \kappa\le\pi_Q(x)=\kappa\le1-\kappa.
\tag{7}
\]
Its H\"older norm is \(\kappa\), so the hypothesis \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\)
gives propensity smoothness.  The control regression is the constant
\(p_*\), whose H\"older norm is at most \(L_\mu/2\), and the contrasts are
zero under \(Q_0\) and \(g_h\) under \(Q_h\), so control-regression and
CATE smoothness follow from the definition of \(p_*\) and (4).  Finally,
the design density equals one almost everywhere, which is exactly
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}design}\).  Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}attainable\text{-}law\text{-}class}\) therefore gives
\[
 Q_0,Q_h\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}.
\tag{8}
\]

Let \(P_0,P_h\) be their one-record observed laws.  The exact calculations
in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}class\text{-}ordinary\text{-}lower}\)
give constants \(C_\chi,C_v\in(0,\infty)\) such that
\[
 \chi^2(P_h\Vert P_0)=C_\chi h^{2\gamma+d},
 \qquad
 \lVert P_h-P_0\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}=C_vh^{\gamma+d},
 \qquad
 \left|\tau_{Q_h}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)
       -\tau_{Q_0}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\right|=a_*h^\gamma.
\tag{9}
\]
That theorem's product-divergence and replacement-private Hamming-transport
steps, using \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), choose constants
\(c_1,c_2\in(0,r_0]\) for which
\[
 h_1=c_1n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)},
 \qquad
 h_2=c_2\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-1}\}^{1/(\gamma+d)}
\tag{10}
\]
have the following property: for every replacement
\((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-private release kernel \(\mathsf K\),
\[
 \lVert P_{h_j}^n\mathsf K-P_0^n\mathsf K\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le1/8,
 \qquad j\in\{1,2\}.
\tag{11}
\]
No full-class honesty premise enters (9)--(11).

Now take any \(C\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\), and let \(\mathsf K\)
be its release kernel.  For either \(h=h_1\) or \(h=h_2\), write
\(\theta_0=\tau_{Q_0}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\),
\(\theta_h=\tau_{Q_h}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\),
\(\nu_0=P_0^n\mathsf K\), and \(\nu_h=P_h^n\mathsf K\).  By (8) and
attainable-class honesty,
\[
 \nu_0\{\theta_0\in C\}\ge1-\eta,
 \qquad
 \nu_h\{\theta_h\in C\}\ge1-\eta.
\tag{12}
\]
Combining (11)--(12) and the union bound gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \nu_0\{\theta_0\in C,\theta_h\in C\}
 &\ge (1-\eta)+(1-\eta-1/8)-1\\
 &=1-2\eta-1/8>3/8,
 \end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
where the final inequality uses \(0<\eta<1/4\).  On the event in (13),
an interval containing both target values has length at least
\(a_*h^\gamma\) by (9).  Hence
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_0}[\operatorname{length}(C)]
 \ge(3a_*/8)h^\gamma.
\tag{14}
\]
Applying (14) at both values in (10), taking their maximum, then taking
the supremum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) and the infimum over
\(C\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\), proves the lower inequality in (1).

For the upper inequality, put
\[
 a_n=1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},
 \qquad
 b_n=1\wedge\left[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}
          \vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\right].
\tag{15}
\]
Choose the deterministic minimizing \((h,k)\) from Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}phase\text{-}sensitive\text{-}expected\text{-}length}\)
and any fixed deterministic pilot dimensions.  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}honest\text{-}private\text{-}pointwise\text{-}interval\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\)
puts the resulting higher-order interval \(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}}\) in
\(\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\), while the phase-sensitive theorem gives
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}})]
 \le C_{\mathrm{HO}}a_n.
\tag{16}
\]
The direct interval \(C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\) in Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}class\text{-}direct\text{-}regression\text{-}upper}\)
is replacement private and honest on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}attainable\text{-}inclusion}\) implies
\[
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\}
 \ge1-\eta
\tag{17}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}\{C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\}]
 \le C_{\mathrm{dir}}b_n.
\tag{18}
\]
Thus both candidates belong to \(\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\).  Equivalently,
one may use the public deterministic selector which releases only
\(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}}\) when \(a_n\le b_n\), and releases only
\(C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\) otherwise.  The selector depends only on public
parameters, runs one mechanism, and hence incurs no privacy composition.
Equations (16)--(18) yield
\[
 \mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}})
 \le \min\{C_{\mathrm{HO}}a_n,C_{\mathrm{dir}}b_n\}
 \le \max\{C_{\mathrm{HO}},C_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\min\{a_n,b_n\},
\tag{19}
\]
which is the upper inequality in (1).

It remains to verify the strict-improvement regime.  Suppose the conditions
following (1) hold.  Since \(q\ge\gamma\), one has \(s=q/2\ge\gamma/2\),
and
\[
 \frac{\gamma}{2}>
 \frac{d/4}{1+d/(2\gamma)}.
\tag{20}
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) and (20) therefore give
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
 \quad
 r_{\mathrm{reg}}=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+d)},
 \quad
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}.
\tag{21}
\]
The first restriction in (2) makes the last term in (21) dominate
\(r_{\mathrm{np}}\), and it also dominates \(r_{\mathrm{reg}}\).  Hence,
for \(n>1\),
\[
 a_n=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}.
\tag{22}
\]
The second restriction in (2) makes the privacy term dominate the sampling
term in \(b_n\), so
\[
 b_n=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\beta/(\beta+d)}.
\tag{23}
\]
Finally, \(\gamma<2\beta\) is equivalent to
\[
 \frac{\beta}{\beta+d}>\frac{\gamma}{\gamma+2d}.
\tag{24}
\]
Equations (22)--(24) imply
\[
 \frac{b_n}{a_n}
 =n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\{\beta/(\beta+d)-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)\}}
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
proving the stated strict polynomial improvement.  All lower and upper
comparisons above are on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\); nothing in the
argument closes the separate full-class open frontier.
added_lemmas.justification: The proposition records the strongest certified two-sided mean-length result on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) by combining the attainable higher-order interval with the restricted full-class direct interval.
added_lemmas.gap: Its ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower endpoint does not determine whether either attainable upper branch is minimax sharp, and it does not close the full-class open frontier.
added_lemmas.consumer: A study designer can use a public rate comparison to select the narrower of two private honest pointwise CATE intervals without paying privacy composition.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper constructs replacement-private, finite-sample honest pointwise CATE intervals on the uniform-design attainable class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  A fully privatized higher-order interval achieves \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\), while the fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval proved on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\) remains valid after restriction to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  A public selector therefore gives the attainable-class upper \(C\min\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},1\wedge[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}]\}\); the same uniform-design witness used for the ordinary full-class lower belongs to the attainable class, yielding the corresponding two-sided nonsharp bracket.  The minimum is a strict polynomial improvement over the higher-order interval in specified privacy-limited regimes.  On the unchanged full class, only the separate ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower and \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper are certified, and the exact private confidence frontier remains open.

project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment for the attainable higher-order construction, proves unrestricted-finite-rank concentration, uniform finite-sample coverage, and the phase-sensitive mean interval length upper \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  It also proves a fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), which restricts to the attainable class.  Combining the two by a public deterministic selector and observing that the ordinary lower-bound witness itself has uniform design gives the best certified attainable-class bracket: under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\), its lower endpoint is \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\) and its upper endpoint is \(C\min\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},1\wedge[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}]\}\).  Separately, the unchanged full class retains its nonsharp ordinary lower versus direct-regression upper bracket; the attainable higher-order upper is not transferred back to that class, and exact full-class sharpness remains unresolved.

prose_updates.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) establish the privacy-free pointwise CATE rate and motivate the higher-order local-polynomial architecture.  Their upper theorem requires its stated design-density and population-Gram conditions; this paper verifies the needed higher-order identities only for its uniform-design attainable construction and does not assert that the KBRW upper transfers to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Nor is KBRW's density-hole fuzzy lower asserted to transfer to the present full class with a positive anchor density band.  On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the paper instead combines its private higher-order interval with its fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval and proves an ordinary two-law lower using witnesses that are themselves uniform-design attainable laws.  The resulting attainable-class bracket is nonsharp but can strictly improve the higher-order upper through deterministic selection.  The separate full-class result remains the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower versus the \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper.  Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective behind the attainable quadratic correction.  Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) motivate honest fixed-length intervals that expose worst-case smoothing bias.  Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) provide nonprivate doubly robust CATE bands in a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem.  Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) study private orthogonal CATE learning but do not derive this pointwise Hölder coverage and length phase; Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) treat private intervals for the regular population ATE.  Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) give an asymptotic resampling conversion for private estimators, whereas the present intervals use explicit uniform finite-sample bias control.  Dwork and Roth (2014) provide the Gaussian mechanism and post-processing fact used by both private constructions.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Settled results are replacement privacy and uniform finite-sample coverage of the explicit higher-order interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), its achieved length upper \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\), the corrected construction-specific privacy-free reduction with no rank floor, and the attainable-class nonsharp minimax bracket obtained by taking the better of that interval and the restricted direct-regression interval.  The bracket's lower witness has uniform design and satisfies every attainable assumption.  The attainable class remains a restricted submodel; its higher-order upper is not transferred to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  On the full class, the settled results are the ordinary lower limitation and the fixed-dimensional direct-regression coverage and upper bound, giving \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le C[1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}]\) under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\).  Whether either bracket is tight, including whether a \(q\)-driven or private-Gram branch is unavoidable, remains unresolved; in particular, the full-class OEQ stays open.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 x=\log(8/\eta),\qquad M=mh^d,\qquad \ell=hk^{-1/d},
\]
and introduce the comparison rates
\[
 r_o=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},\qquad
 r_2=n^{-1/\{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q)\}}.
\tag{1}
\]
The declared domains give \(n\ge 12\), \(d\ge1\), \(q=\alpha+\beta>0\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(0<\eta<1/4\), so every quantity in (1) is well defined and positive.  Since \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\),
\[
 n/4\le m\le n/3.
\tag{2}
\]

We first express the privacy-free rate in a form useful for the construction.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\), together with \(s=q/2\), says that its low-smoothness condition is
\[
 q<\frac{d}{2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}}.
\tag{3}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{2q}>2+\frac d\gamma
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 q<\frac{d}{2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}}.
\tag{4}
\]
For \(n>1\), equations (3)--(4) and the two branches in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) therefore give
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_o\vee r_2.
\tag{5}
\]
At equality in (3) the two quantities in (1) agree, so (5) also covers the boundary.

Define
\[
 R=r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}}
   =r_{\mathrm{up}},
 \qquad
 t=1\wedge R=1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}.
\tag{6}
\]
Fix once and for all a number
\[
 0<t_0<1\wedge r_0^\gamma.
\tag{7}
\]
If \(t<t_0\), then (6)--(7) imply \(t=R\), and (5)--(6) consequently imply
\[
 t\ge r_o,\qquad t\ge r_2,\qquad
 t\ge r_{\mathrm{reg}},\qquad t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}.
\tag{8}
\]

We next reduce the three deterministic envelopes.  For every admissible \(h\) and \(k\), one has \(0<\ell\le h\le r_0\le1/4\).  Hence Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\) and \(\alpha>0\) yield
\[
 \begin{split}
 B(h,k)
 &=C_B\{h^\gamma+\ell^q+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\}\\
 &\le C\{h^\gamma+\ell^q\}.
 \end{split}
\tag{9}
\]
Here and below \(C\in(0,\infty)\) may change from line to line and depends only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\).  Put
\[
 a=M^{-1/2},\qquad b=\frac{\sqrt{k}}{M}.
\tag{10}
\]
The four terms in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\) then give the exact identity
\[
 S(h,k,\eta)
 =C_S\left\{
 \sqrt{x(a^2+b^2)}+xa^2+x^{3/2}ab+x^2b^2
 \right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
In particular, (11) uses no inequality relating \(k\) to \(M\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\), the identity
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}
 =\frac{n\epsilon_n}{\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)\log(1/\eta)}},
\]
and (2) imply
\[
 \begin{split}
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 &\le C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}\{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\}\\
 &=C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}\{h^{-d}+h^{-d}\ell^{-d}\}.
 \end{split}
\tag{12}
\]
Indeed, the remaining logarithmic ratio is
\(\sqrt{\log(8/\eta)/\log(1/\eta)}\), which is finite because \(0<\eta<1/4\), and \(n/m\le4\) by (2).

We now construct an admissible comparison pair when \(t<t_0\).  First suppose \(q<\gamma\), and set
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad
 \ell_0=t^{1/q},\qquad
 K=(h/\ell_0)^d,\qquad
 k=\lceil K\rceil.
\tag{13}
\]
Because \(0<t<1\) and \(q<\gamma\), one has \(K\ge1\).  Therefore
\[
 K\le k\le2K,
 \qquad
 2^{-1/d}\ell_0\le \ell=hk^{-1/d}\le\ell_0.
\tag{14}
\]
Substitution of (13)--(14) into (9), followed by \(t\le1\), gives
\[
 B(h,k)
 \le C\{t+t+t\ell^\alpha\}
 \le Ct.
\tag{15}
\]
By (2), (8), and the definition of \(r_o\) in (1),
\[
 a=m^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}
 \le2n^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}
 \le2t.
\tag{16}
\]
The last inequality in (16) is equivalent to \(t\ge r_o\).  Likewise, (2), (8), (13)--(14), and the definition of \(r_2\) give
\[
 \begin{split}
 b
 &\le \frac{\sqrt2}{m h^{d/2}\ell_0^{d/2}}\\
 &\le4\sqrt2\,n^{-1}t^{-d/(2\gamma)-d/(2q)}
 \le4\sqrt2\,t,
 \end{split}
\tag{17}
\]
where the final inequality is equivalent to \(t\ge r_2\).  Applying \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\le a+b\) to (11), and then using (16)--(17) and \(t\le1\), yields
\[
 S(h,k,\eta)\le C(t+t^2)\le Ct.
\tag{18}
\]

On the branch \(q<\gamma\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) has \(\bar q=q\) and hence gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{reg}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma)},
 \qquad
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)}.
\tag{19}
\]
The last two inequalities in (8), raised to the positive powers displayed in (19), imply
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma}\le t,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma-d/q}\le t.
\tag{20}
\]
Using \(k\le2K\) in (12), and then (13) and (20), proves
\[
 \begin{split}
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 &\le C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}
       \{h^{-d}+h^{-d}\ell_0^{-d}\}\\
 &\le Ct.
 \end{split}
\tag{21}
\]
Combining (15), (18), and (21) gives
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\le Ct.
\tag{22}
\]
The construction (13) remains valid when \(k>M\), because Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\) impose no rank cap.

Now suppose \(q\ge\gamma\), and choose
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad k=1,\qquad \ell=h.
\tag{23}
\]
Since \(h<1\), \(q\ge\gamma\), and \(\alpha>0\), equation (9) yields \(B(h,1)\le Ct\).  Equation (16) still gives \(a\le2t\), whereas (10) and \(k=1\) give \(b=M^{-1}=a^2\le4t^2\).  Substitution in (11), again using \(t\le1\), proves
\[
 S(h,1,\eta)\le Ct.
\tag{24}
\]
Here \(\bar q=\gamma\), so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}
 =N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+2d/\gamma)}.
\tag{25}
\]
Thus \(t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) in (8) is equivalent to
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-2d/\gamma}\le t.
\tag{26}
\]
Because \(h<1\), equations (12), (23), and (26) show
\[
 G(h,1,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 \le C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}h^{-2d}\le Ct.
\tag{27}
\]
Consequently (22) holds on this branch as well.  Equations (19)--(21) exhibit the \(q\)-branch for \(q<\gamma\), while (25)--(27) give the private-Gram rate
\(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}\) for \(q\ge\gamma\).

It remains to verify feasibility and existence of the deterministic minimizer.  In either branch, (8), (13), and (23) imply \(h=t^{1/\gamma}\le t_0^{1/\gamma}<r_0\).  Also, using (2), \(t\ge r_o\), and the definition of \(r_o\),
\[
 mh^d=mt^{d/\gamma}
 \ge\frac14 n^{2\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{28}
\]
Thus, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the comparison pair satisfies the effective-sample constraint \(mh^d\ge C_S^2x\).

For the same sufficiently large \(n\), the feasible bandwidth set is the nonempty compact interval
\[
 I_n=\left[\{C_S^2x/m\}^{1/d},r_0\right].
\tag{29}
\]
For \(h\in I_n\) and integer \(k\ge1\), write
\[
 F_n(h,k)=B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n).
\]
The pair \((r_0,1)\) is feasible for large \(n\), so \(V_n=F_n(r_0,1)<\infty\).  The final, nonnegative term of the sampling envelope and \(h\le r_0\) give
\[
 F_n(h,k)
 \ge \frac{C_Sx^2}{m^2r_0^{2d}}\,k
 =:c_nk,
 \qquad c_n>0.
\tag{30}
\]
No integer \(k>V_n/c_n\) can therefore minimize \(F_n\).  For each of the finitely many remaining integers, the three envelope definitions make \(h\mapsto F_n(h,k)\) continuous on \(I_n\), so the extreme-value theorem gives a minimizer.  Comparing this finite collection yields a global minimizer; lexicographic tie-breaking makes it deterministic.  Denote it by \((\widehat h,\widehat k)\).

When \(t<t_0\), feasibility of the appropriate comparison pair and (22) imply
\[
 F_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\le Ct.
\tag{31}
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) gives, for every sample realization,
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\}
 \le 2F_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\wedge2.
\tag{32}
\]
Thus (31)--(32) bound the length by \(2Ct\) when \(t<t_0\).  When \(t\ge t_0\), truncation to \([-1,1]\) in the same definition gives
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\}
 \le2\le(2/t_0)t.
\tag{33}
\]
The bounds (32)--(33) are pointwise in the sample and independent of \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) and of the deterministic choices \(J_\pi,J_\mu\).  Taking expectation, then the supremum over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), and using (6), proves
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q\!\left[\operatorname{length}\{C_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\}\right]
 \le C_L\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\},
\]
with \(C_L=\max\{2C,2/t_0\}\).  The lower bound on \(n\) used in (28)--(30) depends only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\), which supplies the asserted \(n_0\).  This proof uses only the attainable-class envelopes and supplies no full-class lower or frontier conclusion.
